metadata.title: 1969 Case 09
metadata.original_presentation: A fifty-six-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of fever. She had been well until a month previously, when there was the onset of daily chills and sweats, with elevation of the temperature to between 102 and 104°F.

required.content: What symptoms did the patient experience prior to admission?
required.response: The patient experienced daily chills and sweats, with fever ranging from 102 to 104°F. She had no cough, chest or abdominal pain, dysuria, or urinary frequency.

teaching_points.content: Fever with chills and sweats can indicate an infectious process or inflammatory condition.

required.content: What is the patient's travel and dietary history?
required.response: A year earlier, she had traveled to the southeastern United States. She did not eat pork or drink raw milk.

teaching_points.content: Travel history can provide clues to infectious diseases endemic to certain regions.

required.content: What were the patient's previous medical evaluations and treatments?
required.response: She had been taking exercises for stiffness of the thigh muscles but had experienced no articular discomfort. Previous tests included negative heterophil-agglutination and agglutination tests for typhoid, paratyphoid, and brucella. Four L.E.-cell tests were negative.

teaching_points.content: Negative serological tests can help rule out specific infectious diseases.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Malaria
supporting_evidence: travel to southeastern United States (possible exposure)
refuting_evidence: no specific travel to known malaria-endemic regions mentioned

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Brucellosis
refuting_evidence: no consumption of raw milk or pork

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Endocarditis
supporting_evidence: persistent fever with chills and sweats
refuting_evidence: no mention of heart murmur or predisposing heart conditions

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lymphoma
refuting_evidence: no mention of weight loss or lymphadenopathy

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Rheumatic fever
refuting_evidence: no history of recent sore throat or streptococcal infection

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: No rash or petechiae were seen on the skin or mucosal surfaces. The lungs were clear, cardiac sounds were normal, and no murmur or friction rub was heard. The abdomen was soft with no tenderness or palpable mass. There was slight fusiform deformity of the interphalangeal joints of the hands.

teaching_points.content: Physical examination can reveal signs of systemic disease, such as joint deformities or skin changes.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
supporting_evidence: slight fusiform deformity of the interphalangeal joints

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
supporting_evidence: slight fusiform deformity of the interphalangeal joints

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Brucellosis
additional_information_needed: repeat brucella serology, consider PCR for brucella

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Malaria
additional_information_needed: thick and thin blood smears for malaria parasites

required.content: What were the results of the initial laboratory tests?
required.response: Urinalysis was negative; hematocrit was 37%, white-cell count 3000 with 47% neutrophils, 26% band forms, 26% lymphocytes, and 1% basophils. Culture of the urine grew proteus organisms; numerous blood cultures yielded no growth.

teaching_points.content: Laboratory tests can help identify infections and hematological abnormalities.

required.content: What imaging studies were performed and what were their results?
required.response: X-ray films of the chest and intravenous pyelograms were normal. An upper gastrointestinal series was normal except for a small hiatus hernia and a duodenal diverticulum.

teaching_points.content: Imaging studies can help rule out structural abnormalities and identify incidental findings.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Infective Endocarditis
supporting_evidence: persistent fever with chills and sweats

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
supporting_evidence: slight fusiform deformity of interphalangeal joints
refuting_evidence: no rash or other systemic symptoms

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
supporting_evidence: slight fusiform deformity of interphalangeal joints

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: Buffered aspirin, 2.4 gm daily, was administered, which decreased the temperature to 100°F. Aspirin therapy was resumed on the fourteenth hospital day, and the patient remained afebrile thereafter.

teaching_points.content: Aspirin can be used to manage fever and inflammation.
